title: POC scoping: open models shortlist - Cortexa
summary: POC scoping call to align success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines, and shortlist open models for Cortexa's multilingual domain QA workload. Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs, private vs hosted, security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS), and next steps to run benchmarks on 3 candidate models.
next_steps: Redwood to share POC pricing matrix and recommended instance configs (Maya) by 2026-04-27
Customer to provide sample dataset (50-100 queries in EN/FR/DE) and evaluation rubric by 2026-04-29
Schedule benchmark run and review session w/ SE (Ravi) week of 2026-05-04
action_items: Maya Chen: Send POC pricing + config options and sample benchmark template by 2026-04-27
Lena Ortiz: Share representative multilingual sample dataset (approx 100 queries) by 2026-04-29
Ravi Patel: Prepare benchmark harness and run initial latency/throughput tests against shortlist by 2026-05-05
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and Ravi is our SE.
[00:00:12] Lena: Hi, Lena here, Head of ML at Cortexa. Ben and Amir are on as well.
[00:00:20] Ben: Hey all.
[00:00:22] Amir: Morning.
[00:00:25] Maya: Cool. Objective for today: lock success criteria for the POC, get sizing and bench plan, and agree on open model shortlist. We're aware you need multilingual support, mainly English, French, German and some domain questions for healthcare-adjacent docs.
[00:00:45] Lena: Yep that's right. Our primary use case is customer support knowledge base QA and some triage—short answers and document retrieval, sometimes long context. Latency under 400ms p95 ideally, but we'll tolerate up to 700ms depending on cost.
[00:01:05] Ravi: Got it. Quick clarifying q, when you say latency target is that for single-request generation or end-to-end with retrieval?
[00:01:12] Lena: For single-request generation with a 2k token context. Retrieval adds a bit but we mostly want generation SLAs.
[00:01:20] Ben: Also important—data can't leave EU for some of our clients; we need EU region or Private deployment. SOC2 is required, and we'd like support for SSO/SAML and customer KMS.
[00:01:34] Maya: That's fine. Redwood Private can be deployed in your VPC, or we can run dedicated capacity in EU regions. Both support KMS and SAML integrations; we'll share the security pack.
[00:01:45] Amir: Cost is a factor. We're evaluating open models to avoid heavy token costs of hosted closed models.
[00:01:52] Ravi: For open models we typically recommend a shortlist balancing cost and quality. Based on your multilingual + domain needs, our initial shortlist is: Llama-2-70B-chat (quantized variants), MPT-30B-Instruct, and Falcon-40B-Instruct (or Falcon-40B-qa variant). We'll also include a smaller Llama-2-13B as a baseline for throughput/cost.
[00:02:18] Lena: Quick Q: do you run quantized kernels? How much quality loss should we expect?
[00:02:25] Ravi: We run int8 and INT4-like quant profiles for LLMs; quality loss depends on prompt complexity. For instruction-following, 13B in int8 may be fine for high-throughput, but for nuanced multilingual QA 70B quantized often performs better. We'll surface token-level diffs in the benchmark.
[00:02:42] Ben: Also, can you simulate our traffic? We have spikes—approx 200 qps for short bursts. Steady-state maybe 40-60 rps.
[00:02:51] Maya: We'll size for your 200 qps burst using Dedicated pools + autoscale, and also show a hosted latency/cost comparison.
[00:02:58] Amir: Timeline? We want results in 2-3 weeks if possible.
[00:03:03] Maya: Okay we propose: week 1 data handoff and config; week 2 run benchmarks; week 3 analyze and present. So about 2-3 weeks.
[00:03:12] Ravi: For benchmarks, metrics we'll collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (rps), tokens/sec, cost-per-1k-tokens estimate, and qualitative accuracy on rubric. We'll also capture multi-lingual parity per-lang.
[00:03:27] Lena: Accuracy rubric—we'll provide gold answers for the sample queries. We'll score exact match and partial credit for synonyms.
[00:03:35] Maya: Great, please send the sample set. We'll also ask for a couple of hard domain prompts.
[00:03:41] Ben: Security follow-ups: can you provide SOC2 docs and architecture diagram for Private?
[00:03:46] Maya: Yes, we'll drop the security pack link in the notes: https://redwood.test/security-pack (note: auto-link placeholder).
[00:03:55] Ravi: A few technical notes: for long-context 2k tokens we might enable KV caching to reduce repeated context cost, and for multilingual we may prefer models pre-trained on diverse corpora — Falcon tends to do well on European languages but sometimes lags on certain domain jargon; Llama-2-70B typically better but higher cost.
[00:04:18] Amir: Any limitations for on-prem? Our infra team prefers VMs vs Kubernetes.
[00:04:23] Ravi: We support both—there's an on-prem package that runs on k8s or a VM appliance; we'll include deployment options in the doc. Some kernel optimizations need NVIDIA drivers and certain CUDA versions, we'll list those.
[00:04:36] Lena: Good. For success criteria, we want: 1) p95 latency < 700ms on 2k context, 2) accuracy >= 85% on gold set, 3) cost projection under $X per 1M tokens (we'll set threshold after we get pricing).
[00:04:52] Maya: Sounds reasonable. We'll return a recommended config per model with expected costs and expected latency.
[00:04:58] Amir: Any thoughts on reranking vs single-shot generation? We might do simple rerank with embeddings for top-5 then generate.
[00:05:06] Ravi: That's recommended for QA scale — use smaller embedding model + rerank then generate with larger model. We can include an inference pipeline config in the POC.
[00:05:14] Lena: About evaluation, we want multilingual parity checks (EN/FR/DE) and domain-specific edge cases.
[00:05:20] Maya: We'll run per-lang metrics. Also will include sample prompts and temperature settings.
[00:05:26] Ben: Are there any gotchas with quantized 70B on NV60 class GPUs?
[00:05:31] Ravi: Performance depends on kernels; our runtime picks kernels per-hardware. Quantized 70B can run on A10/NV60-ish hardware with higher latency; for p95 targets you might want A100 / H100 for lowest latency. We'll show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[00:05:46] Lena: Ok. Anything else?
[00:05:48] Maya: Recap of next steps: Maya sends pricing + security pack; Lena sends dataset and rubric; Ravi sets up benchmark harness and schedules run. We'll target review on 2026-05-06.
[00:06:02] Amir: Works for us.
[00:06:05] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the benchmark review.
[00:06:10] [call ends]

Notes: transcription has some small mis-hearings (Falcon often transcribed as "Falkon" in other calls), speaker labels may have slight mismatches. References: security doc link (placeholder), sample benchmark template (will be shared).
